regime_context: The detector shows Big Banks as the clear leader (score 1.018, durability_bar 0.8, breadth 1.0, uncrowded) with Oil & Gas as the only challenger but ineligible (durability 0.23, breadth 0.214). Rotation is broad (9/16 eligible), not one-narrative, and non-directional. Track record is weak: hit rate 55.8% but directional accuracy is only 31.3% — past directional calls underperformed coin-flip, so conviction should lean low. emerging_watch: Watching Oil & Gas Producers (XEG.TO): the challenger score (0.915) is close to Big Banks' lead, but durability is weak (0.23) and breadth is thin (0.214). If XEG.TO's score overtakes ZEB.TO AND its breadth expands above 0.6, that would retire this watch as a confirmed handoff.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only theme with a strong, confirmed leadership profile: rank 1, high durability (0.8), full breadth (1.0), trend-regime hurst, and uncrowded (z=0.7). The absolute-trend gate (the one validated leg) supports staying with the trend until it breaks, not adding. This is a stay-with-the-leader lean driven by durability/breadth, not a momentum-buy call.
theses.dissent: Canadian banks often mean-revert around macro/rate cycles; high breadth can mark late-stage extension, and the challenger (Oil & Gas) is close in score, suggesting a fragile lead.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO lags XEG.TO by 5% over the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Consumer Staples & Retail shows the strongest combination of durability (0.82) and breadth (1.0) among eligible themes outside the leader, with a trend hurst tag. It is eligible and uncrowded. This is a secondary quality-trend lean, not a rank-based buy.
theses.dissent: Defensive staples leadership in Canada can be a market-rotation artifact rather than a durable alpha source; it may lag cyclicals if risk appetite picks up.

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
